title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it uses artificial intelligence in its services and decisions, so veterans and the public can see and understand the technology behind care and benefits. The law mandates clear reporting, accountability measures, and safeguards to protect veteran privacy while ensuring AI systems are explained in plain language and regularly audited for fairness and accuracy.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act mandates that the Department of Veterans Affairs must use artificial‑intelligence tools responsibly when reviewing and adjudicating veterans’ claims, ensuring decisions are transparent and explainable. It establishes requirements for auditing AI systems, protecting claimant rights, and providing clear recourse for veterans if AI‑driven determinations are found to be unfair or inaccurate.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect electoral integrity by setting rules that limit how AI tools can create and spread deceptive or misleading content during voting periods. It establishes safeguards, monitoring requirements, and penalties to curb AI‑generated misinformation that could influence or distort voter decisions.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes federal guidelines to ensure that AI systems developed and tested in the United States are safe, transparent, and reliable. It creates a review board, sets testing standards, and mandates data privacy and accountability for AI research projects.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This Act aims to safeguard consumers by requiring clear labeling and disclosure of AI-generated content to prevent deception. It establishes penalties for companies that misrepresent AI usage and mandates transparency in AI products and services.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to establish comprehensive security protocols for AI systems, ensuring they are resilient against threats and misuse. It promotes collaboration between government and industry to develop standards, testing, and oversight to protect national security and public trust.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to identify and mitigate risks posed by AI systems that could affect national security and critical infrastructure. It directs the task force to collaborate with industry, academia, and other government agencies to develop secure AI standards, guidelines, and best practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act aims to regulate the use of artificial intelligence to prevent risks and protect public safety. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and enforcement mechanisms for developers and users of AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a proposed law that establishes a framework for the coordination, oversight, and safety of autonomous physical AI systems such as robots, drones, and other automated devices. It requires manufacturers and operators to register their systems, follow standardized safety protocols, and report incidents to a central regulatory body to protect public safety and maintain accountability.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The bill amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to require any political advertisement that contains AI‑generated images or video to include a clear disclosure statement. This change is intended to increase transparency and accountability in political advertising by making it clear when generative AI is used.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating AI tools that could spread misinformation or manipulate voter perceptions. The legislation seeks to establish guidelines and oversight for AI-generated content in political contexts to ensure transparency and prevent electoral interference.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes a framework for overseeing artificial intelligence systems that can autonomously modify their own behavior. It requires regular reporting, safety checks, and regulatory compliance to prevent unintended consequences and ensure these systems act in ways that align with societal values.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation aimed at preventing artificial intelligence systems from acting in harmful or unintended ways. It would establish strict safety standards, monitoring protocols, and penalties for developers and operators who fail to comply.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. Its purpose is to allow policymakers to assess environmental, economic, and societal impacts before permitting further development.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with overseeing investigations related to cybersecurity and AI, aiming to protect national security and sensitive data. The act details the board’s authority, responsibilities, and cooperation with other agencies to prevent and respond to cyber threats involving AI.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit U.S. citizens, focusing on economic growth, job creation, and public trust. It seeks to encourage responsible innovation by establishing guidelines, fostering collaboration between government and industry, and protecting American interests in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and organizations developing or using artificial intelligence to submit regular reports on the computational power, energy consumption, and environmental impact of their AI systems. The act aims to increase transparency, promote energy efficiency, and ensure that AI development aligns with national sustainability and security goals.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that only licensed human doctors may diagnose and treat patients, preventing artificial intelligence from making medical decisions on its own. It aims to protect patient safety and maintain professional standards by requiring all medical care to involve qualified healthcare professionals.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy establishes a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office to monitor and address risks from AI and other advanced technologies. It also includes additional measures and responsibilities related to these emerging tech threats.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to guide and oversee AI-related policy, research, and regulation. The committee will coordinate efforts among stakeholders to ensure responsible development and deployment of AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 is a proposed law that would establish a framework for assessing the risks associated with AI systems before they are deployed. It aims to require developers to conduct thorough risk analyses and to report findings to regulators, ensuring that potential safety, privacy, and societal impacts are identified and managed early in the AI development process.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a legislative framework aimed at ensuring the safe, ethical, and responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and accountability measures to protect public interests, privacy, and societal welfare.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law designed to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems by setting standards for energy use, carbon emissions, and waste management. It requires companies to monitor, report, and minimize the ecological impacts of AI development, deployment, and disposal.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a law that requires schools to teach students about artificial intelligence, so they can use it safely and understand how it works. It will provide funding, set curriculum standards, train teachers, and supply tools to prepare students and educators for the growing role of AI in society and the workforce.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 establishes federal guidelines to ensure AI systems are developed safely, transparently, and responsibly. It sets standards for research, testing, and deployment, and creates oversight mechanisms to protect public safety, privacy, and the integrity of AI technologies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It aims to test and showcase AI‑driven defense capabilities as part of the nation’s cybersecurity strategy.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a federal law that requires schools to teach students basic concepts about artificial intelligence and how AI can be used responsibly. It also provides funding and guidance for teachers, schools, and communities to build the skills and knowledge needed to safely and effectively integrate AI technology into everyday learning.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act aims to increase public understanding of artificial intelligence by launching nationwide educational and awareness campaigns. It seeks to provide resources, training, and outreach to help people make informed decisions about AI technology.
